scenario: a second start() arms a second tick interval, and stop() leaves one running
reason: Owner-approved 2026-11-01 (decisions page row s): in 1.35 every start() arms a new tick interval, even while the system is running or after destroy(), and keeps only the newest handle, so ticks multiply and an older interval keeps firing after stop() or destroy(); 2.0 arms the tick only on a start() that starts the system, and stop() and destroy() clear it. In this scenario s1's first attach calls system.stop(); s0 is attached before it, s2 and the gated g after it. 2.0 detaches s1 at once (a detach and an unsubscribe) and never attaches s2 (no subscribe and no attach); 1.35 leaves s1 and s2 attached, which the inspect snapshots in steps 2 and 3 show. This covers the "stopped inside an attach" checkpoint's inspect snapshot, where the value at inspect.sources[2].attached differs in step 3 (1.35: true, 2.0: false). Signed 2026-11-01 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve both", 2026-11-01) and asked Claude to sign for him.

scenario: async stop, evict and destroy
reason: GATE-1 quirk j (L3): after stop() then start(), 1.35 does not run still-wanted canceled requirements again; 2.0's start() re-dispatches every requirement still wanted. This covers the onReconcileEnd hook call, where the value at args[0].inflight[0] differs in step 4. scenario: a batch that satisfied A by its own write, with A raised again while it runs: A completes twice, from the old batch and the new run, with no cancel (au)
kind: the batch [A, B] has satisfied both (30 ms)
reason: Row (as) (L7; owner-approved 2026-11-05, "Approve (Recommended)"): settle(), the settled notification and inspect() count a running batch, so settle() waits for batched work and inspect() lists a running batch's requirements in flight. 1.35 resolves settle() without waiting for the batches it started and lists no batch in flight (L7 RFC C6, probe B7). The approved risks: a fake-timer test that awaits settle() during a batch wait waits until the timers advance, and a batch longer than 5 s with no timeoutMs makes settle() reject. In this scenario the batch [A, B] satisfies A by its own write and A is raised again while the batch runs: 2.0's old batch reports a cancel for A when A's new run supersedes it, and A completes once, from the new run; 1.35 reports no cancel and completes A twice, once from the old batch (the records 2.0 lacks) and once from the new run. This record is one of the checkpoint's inspect() fields, taken while a batch runs: 2.0 lists the batch's requirements in flight (inflight and resolvers), 1.35 lists none. This covers the state "the batch [A, B] has satisfied both (30 ms)" record in step 2, which differs at inspect.inflight[0]. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve (Recommended)", 2026-11-05) and asked Claude to sign for him.

In this scenario batch is enabled with only resolve(): 2.0 starts each of the three requirements as an ordinary run when the window closes, so the resolver-start records and the reconcile report's in-flight list show them; 1.35 runs each on a private controller, with no start record. This covers the hook "onReconcileEnd" record in step 2, which differs at args[0].inflight[1]. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve all (Recommended)", 2026-11-05) and asked Claude to sign for him.

scenario: retracting one requirement of a running batch cancels all of it, and the still-wanted ones never run again (U2)
reason: Row (as) (L7; owner-approved 2026-11-05, "Approve (Recommended)"): settle(), the settled notification and inspect() count a running batch, so settle() waits for batched work and inspect() lists a running batch's requirements in flight. 1.35 resolves settle() without waiting for the batches it started and lists no batch in flight (L7 RFC C6, probe B7). The approved risks: a fake-timer test that awaits settle() during a batch wait waits until the timers advance, and a batch longer than 5 s with no timeoutMs makes settle() reject. In this scenario b is retracted from the running batch [a, b, c] at 30 ms: 2.0 cancels b alone, the signal stays clean, and a and c complete at 70 ms. This record is one of the checkpoint's inspect() fields, taken while a batch runs: 2.0 lists the batch's requirements in flight (inflight and resolvers), 1.35 lists none. This covers the state "running" record in step 3, which differs at inspect.inflight[0]. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve (Recommended)", 2026-11-05) and asked Claude to sign for him.

scenario: retracting one requirement of a running batch cancels all of it, and the still-wanted ones never run again (U2)
reason: GATE-1 quirk g (L7): retracting one requirement of a running batch cancels only that requirement. 1.35 aborts the whole batch and cancels every requirement in it, and declares that intended ("you can't abort one row of a SQL UPDATE without aborting the transaction", resolvers.ts 2131-2136); the still-wanted ones are never run again, which is 1.35's general rule for a canceled requirement that is still wanted, the same as row j (L7 RFC C2; verified in probe B2 and again in the design review's rerun: b retracted from [a, b, c] mid-run, the signal aborted, a, b and c each canceled, the handler not run again, a and c left unmet). 2.0 cancels the retracted requirement alone; the batch keeps running for the rest and drops its outcome report for the retracted one; resolveBatch writes facts directly, so the facts it already wrote are not undone; the batch's signal aborts only when every requirement has left. In this scenario b is retracted from the running batch [a, b, c] at 30 ms: 2.0 cancels b alone, the signal stays clean, and a and c complete at 70 ms. This covers the hook "onResolverCancel" record in step 6, which differs at args[1].id. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row at GATE-1 ("Approved gates and go with your recommendation: but needs to be correct not a patch or monkey fix", 2026-10-30), approved Claude signing L7's entries ("Approve all (Recommended)", 2026-11-05), and asked Claude to sign for him.

reason: GATE-1 quirk g (L7): retracting one requirement of a running batch cancels only that requirement. 1.35 aborts the whole batch and cancels every requirement in it, and declares that intended ("you can't abort one row of a SQL UPDATE without aborting the transaction", resolvers.ts 2131-2136); the still-wanted ones are never run again, which is 1.35's general rule for a canceled requirement that is still wanted, the same as row j (L7 RFC C2; verified in probe B2 and again in the design review's rerun: b retracted from [a, b, c] mid-run, the signal aborted, a, b and c each canceled, the handler not run again, a and c left unmet). 2.0 cancels the retracted requirement alone; the batch keeps running for the rest and drops its outcome report for the retracted one; resolveBatch writes facts directly, so the facts it already wrote are not undone; the batch's signal aborts only when every requirement has left. scenario: fuzz
reason: GATE-1 quirk j (L3), its batch path (L7): a restart (stop() then start()) re-dispatches a requirement that is still wanted, so 2.0 runs its resolver again where 1.35 does not. 1.35 keeps the requirement in its previous set across stop() (core engine.ts, the reconcile diff and `state.previousRequirements = currentSet`), so the pass after start() sees nothing added and never calls resolve() again; 2.0's stop_() records the canceled ids and start() re-dispatches them (core-next api/reconcile.ts, `restart`). For a batched resolver the re-dispatch queues the requirement, and the call starts from the queue's window with no onResolverStart hook and before any later reconcile pass, so its first record is the handler's external "start" record ([kind, tag "<module>.rb", call number, the call's items]), which the group's other entries do not match (fuzz seed 8 at forced L11, shrunk to one batched source: stop, then start). From the re-dispatch on, the case runs differently, so this entry ends the fuzz case (`ends`), only in a case with a stop followed by a start and no destroy (`when: restart`), as the group's other entries do. Signed 2026-11-17 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row on the decisions page ("If all are better or non user facing they are all approved") and asked Claude to sign for him.

reason: Row (bc) (L8; the L8 RFC, "an import with a bad index fails"): 2.0 rejects a history import whose `currentIndex` is outside its snapshot list, and logs 1.35's own import failure, "[Directive] Failed to import history data:", with the reason "currentIndex must be the index of a snapshot"; 1.35 imports it. The fuzz reaches it when a `roundtrip` exports a history that holds no snapshot (`currentIndex` -1). The `importedEmpty` trigger names one way to get there (a module with `snapshotEvents`); the L11 data-form phase found another (fuzz seed 5 at L11: a module with a template compute and no `snapshotEvents`, whose history is still empty at the roundtrip on both engines). So `when` is `imported` (history on and a roundtrip), and the bound names only this record: an error whose first argument is the import-failure text word for word (`historyImportFailed`) and whose second is the error object with (bc)'s own reason word for word, "[Directive] Invalid history data: currentIndex must be the index of a snapshot" (`historyIndexNotASnapshot`, read before the contract's mask), so any other import failure stays unexplained. The case runs the same after it (the import changes nothing on either engine), so the entry does not end it. Signed 2026-11-18 on the owner's instruction (GATE-2 rule 1): "Approve all as recommended (Recommended)" (2026-11-10), which approved row (bc).

reason: Row (as) (L7a, #357): 2.0's `settle()` counts a running batch and waits for it, where 1.35's resolves while it runs. 1.35's own settle() runs every queue at each settled change while it waits (engine.ts:4070-4073, processBatches), and 2.0 keeps that rule (api/batch.ts `kernel.define("batch")`, called from settle's onSettledChange listener). So in a settle step whose batch is still running, a requirement queued behind a `maxSize` flush (the overflow item) is started at the next settled change on 2.0, where 1.35's settle has already returned and the item waits out its window (resolvers.ts:1888-1902). 1.35 then makes one more reconcile pass than 2.0. Pinned with the public API (fix2/shrink/u7.mjs and u7-held.mjs): with an unbatched 40 ms resolver holding 1.35's settle() open as well, 1.35 starts the overflow call at once, as 2.0 does, and both make the same passes. PR seed 7 at L11 (spec u7). This covers a reconcile pass on 1.35 only and ends the case (`ends`): every later record of the step is shifted by the missing pass. Signed 2026-11-19 on the owner's instruction ("Yes, run 5 (Recommended)", 2026-11-19), in the L11 gate run 5: he approved row (as) ("Approve (Recommended)", 2026-11-05), approved Claude signing L7's entries ("Approve all (Recommended)", 2026-11-05), and "I approve you for to do everything" (2026-11-15).
